problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})={x}^{2}+3x+5$ and $L({y}_{2})=x+2$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L({y}_{1}-3{y}_{2})?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})=4x$ and $L({y}_{2})={x}^{2}+1$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2})?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
L(a{y}_{1}(x)+b{y}_{2}(x))=aL({y}_{1}(x))+bL({y}_{2}(x))
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L({y}_{1}-2{y}_{2}) & =L({y}_{1})-2L({y}_{2}) \\  & =4x-2({x}^{2}+1) \\  & =-2{x}^{2}+4x-2 \\  & =-2({x}^{2}-2x+1) \\  & =-2(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
